topic: Machine-level Programming with x86-64 Assembly and Jump Tables
explanation: This concept involves understanding how high-level language constructs translate into low-level assembly instructions, particularly focusing on efficient implementations using techniques like jump tables.  Jump tables are crucial for optimizing switch statements, improving performance by directly jumping to the correct code section based on the input value, avoiding sequential comparisons.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
.rodata
.align 8
JUMP_TABLE:
    .quad CASE_0
    .quad CASE_1
    .quad DEFAULT_CASE

.text
.globl switch_func
switch_func:
    MOVQ %rdi, %rax         ; Input index (i) in RAX
    CMPQ $2, %rax           ; Check bounds (Max index 2)
    JA DEFAULT_CASE

    JMP *JUMP_TABLE(,%rax, 8) ; Indirect Jump: TABLE + (i * 8)

CASE_0:
    MOV $10, %eax
    RET
CASE_1:
    MOV $20, %eax
    RET
DEFAULT_CASE:
    MOV $-1, %eax
    RET
keywords: Jump Table, x86 switch optimization, Indirect jump
